Check herdr.dev for new Herdr versions in the background.
Check herdr.dev for remote agent-detection manifest updates in the background. Bundled manifests and local overrides still apply.

Modifier combo for workspace shortcuts 1-9. Unset by default.
Modifier combo for agent shortcuts 1-9. Unset by default.
Open a new chat tab in the home directory with the default chat agent. Unset by default.
Toggle the native file manager.
Open the focused-agent attachment picker.
Accent color for highlights, borders, and navigation UI. Accepts hex (#89b4fa), named colors (cyan, blue), or RGB (rgb(137,180,250)).
Agent sidebar ordering. Saved values are "spaces" or "priority"; "workspaces" is accepted as an alias for "spaces".

How workspace chat drawers open and close. "all-active" keeps a drawer open for every workspace with a live agent, "focused" follows the active workspace around, and "manual" only obeys the disclosure clicks.
Ask for confirmation before closing a workspace.
Copy text selected with the mouse.
Labels the daily chat section leaves out. Accepted labels are "context", "project", and "routine"; an empty list brings every chat back.
Hide the tab row when the workspace has one tab.
Host cursor policy.
Terminal width at or below which Herdr uses the mobile single-column layout.
Capture mouse input for Herdr's mouse UI.
Lines to scroll per mouse wheel notch.

Which surfaces let the vertical wheel scroll Herdr's own scrollback over a pane that asked for mouse reporting. "mobile" is the phone shell only, where a swipe is the only scroll gesture there is. "scrollable" extends it to every surface, so an agent that reports the wheel and then ignores it no longer leaves the content area looking frozen — at the cost of panes that do act on the wheel without an alternate screen, which stop receiving it. "never" always hands the wheel to the pane. No value overrides the scrollback guard: a pane Herdr has no scrollback for, such as any full-screen program, keeps its wheel in every mode.
Draw borders around split panes.
Keep split panes visually separated instead of sharing divider borders.
Ask for a tab name before creating a new tab.
Ask for a workspace name before interactive TUI creation.
Force a full host-terminal redraw when the outer terminal regains focus.

Modifier that lets right-click gestures pass through to pane apps. Empty disables it. Accepts ctrl, alt, cmd, super, meta, hyper, or a + separated combination; shift is rejected because many terminals reserve Shift+mouse.

Structural markers that say a chat was opened by an automation rather than by a person, matched against the start of the chat's first message: a marker that only appears mid-sentence is a mention, not a declaration.

Further openings that mark a chat as routine, matched as a prefix of the first message once case and spacing are normalised. Which chores repeat is a fact about your work rather than about Herdr, so this list ships empty.
How many chats must share one opening before the repetition alone marks them routine. 0 turns that rule off and leaves the markers and patterns working.
Show agent labels in split pane borders when no manual pane label is set.
Frame tone for the agents half. Same vocabulary as the shell bars: a palette token follows the theme, anything else is a literal colour.
Draw a rounded frame around the agents half of the left panel. It costs two cells on each axis of that half.
Two or more stops to fade the agents frame between along its long axis. Both ends must carry channel values.
Blank terminal rows between expanded Agent sidebar entries. Set to 1 to restore the previous spacing.

Default expanded Agent sidebar layout. Entries may be token strings or inline { token, fg, bold, dim } style tables. Supports built-in and $name metadata tokens; at most 16 rows and 16 tokens per row.
Complete Agent-row overrides keyed by strict canonical agent id. Agents without an override use ui.sidebar.agents.rows.
Frame tone for the left panel's own controls. Same vocabulary as the shell bars: a palette token follows the theme, anything else is a literal colour.
Draw the left panel's controls as small framed buttons. The footer grows from one row to three to hold them, and controls that cannot fit a frame keep their plain labels.
Two or more stops to fade the control frames between along their long axis. Both ends must carry channel values.
Frame tone for the spaces half. Same vocabulary as the shell bars: a palette token follows the theme, anything else is a literal colour.
Draw a rounded frame around the spaces half of the left panel. It costs two cells on each axis of that half.
Two or more stops to fade the spaces frame between along its long axis. Both ends must carry channel values.

Start new clients with the Spaces tree focused: only the checkout being worked in and the ones running an agent, with the modules above them. The footer's focus switch toggles it live, per display; this is only where a display begins.
Blank terminal rows between expanded Space sidebar entries. Set to 1 to restore the previous spacing. Consecutive indented worktree children remain packed as one group.
Expanded Space sidebar layout. Entries may be token strings or inline { token, fg, bold, dim } style tables. Supports built-in and $name metadata tokens; at most 16 rows and 16 tokens per row.
Collapsed sidebar presentation.
Maximum sidebar width (columns) when expanded.
Minimum sidebar width (columns) when expanded.
Start Herdr with the sidebar collapsed. Changes take effect on the next launch.
Default expanded sidebar width in columns. Auto-scales based on workspace names.

Colour of the heavy vertical seam between the sidebar and the stage. Palette token (accent, peach, red, ...) or a literal colour, the same vocabulary as shell bar colours. Navigate mode always paints the seam accent.
Absolute (or `~`-rooted) project directories pinned to the Projects tab. Blank and non-absolute entries are dropped from the usable set and reported as diagnostics instead of failing the config load.
Agent CLI id used for new chats opened from the Projects tab. Unknown values fall back to claude at launch, so a stale entry cannot break the "+" button.
List only chats that are open as tabs in the Projects tab (the footer "actives" toggle). Defaults to on when absent.
Glyph drawn before a project header's name when the [[spaces.project]] entry has no icon of its own. Empty disables the glyph.
Glyph drawn before workspace (branch/checkout) rows in the Spaces tree. The default is the Powerline git-branch glyph (U+E0A0); set a plain glyph if your font lacks it. Empty disables the glyph.
Glyph drawn before chat rows in a workspace's chat drawer. Empty disables the glyph.
Glyph drawn before the daily area's header — the chats no checkout claims. A home rather than a speech bubble: that row names a place, not a conversation. Empty disables the glyph.

Whether a declared [[spaces.split]] rule that currently claims no open checkout still draws its (dim) header in the sidebar tree, with an (empty) row beneath. Set false to hide memberless rules until a matching branch is open.
How the wired browser preview places itself when a chat tab gains focus. Only same-screen-half is implemented; the announced modes behave like the default at runtime.
Popup notification delivery. off disables popups, herdr shows in-app toasts, terminal asks the outer terminal for a desktop notification, system asks the OS notification service directly.

Seconds to wait before sending finished or needs-input agent notifications. Herdr notifies only if the pane is still in the same state when the delay expires. 0 is instant; valid values are 0 through 3600.
In-app toast position, relative to the full Herdr frame.
Show the copied-to-clipboard popup after a mouse copy.
Copied-to-clipboard popup position.
Play sounds when agents change state in background workspaces.

Optional mp3 file path for "done" notifications. Relative paths are resolved from the config file's directory.

Resume supported AI-agent panes into their native conversation sessions when restoring a Herdr session.

Let each attached display hold its own workspace, tab and focused pane so several monitors can watch different tabs of one session at the same time. Set to false to mirror one view onto every display.
Root directory under which Herdr creates <repo>/<branch-slug> checkouts.
Add keepalive fallbacks and private connection reuse for `herdr --remote`. Set false to run plain ssh unchanged.
Maximum scrollback buffer size in bytes retained per pane terminal. The legacy key name `scrollback_lines` is accepted as an alias.
Allow launching herdr inside an existing herdr pane.
Experimental local Kitty graphics rendering for attached clients.
Persist pane screen history to session-history.json.

Automatically put retired panes to sleep: a pane whose child process has exited and that no display is watching gets its scrollback written to disk and its runtime released after a quiet period. Touching the pane wakes it with its history replayed. Panes with a running process are never touched.

Let an idle server exit: when no client is attached and no pane has a running process for a grace period, the server writes every retired pane's scrollback to disk, saves the session, and stops. The next `herdr` start restores the session with that history.

Expose the focused pane's cursor anchor to the outer terminal even when the pane requested `?25l`, so macOS native input methods keep tracking the candidate window when TUIs paint their own cursor (Claude Code, pi, codex, etc.). Default: false.  When the pane reports no cursor position, falls back to the pane's top-left so a stable IME anchor is always available.  Trade-off when enabled: an extra hardware cursor will be visible in the outer terminal for apps that hide the cursor without painting a replacement (vim normal mode, etc.). See #149.

Restrict `reveal_hidden_cursor_for_cjk_ime` to focused panes whose detected agent matches one of these names (case-insensitive). Empty list means apply to any focused pane. Unknown agent names are ignored; if the list contains no valid names, the reveal does not apply. Accepted names: pi, claude, codex, gemini, cursor, devin, cline, opencode, copilot, kimi, kiro, droid, amp, grok, hermes, kilo, qodercli, qoder, maki.
Cursor shape rendered for the IME anchor when `reveal_hidden_cursor_for_cjk_ime` is enabled.

While prefix mode is active, temporarily switch the macOS host input source to an ASCII-capable keyboard layout so prefix commands are read as ASCII even when a CJK IME is active, then restore the previous input source when prefix mode exits. macOS only; a no-op elsewhere and a best-effort no-op if the switch fails.

Devices pinned to the top of the file manager send picker, in order. Each entry is a tailnet DNS name (for example "laptop.tailnet.ts.net"), because host names can repeat. Written by pressing p in the picker.

The look this bar wears when its parts do not say otherwise: framed draws the bar's own panel, islands frames each section instead, plain draws neither. It only fills in unwritten border keys — anything written explicitly wins.
Draw the bottom bar as a bordered panel with rounded corners.

Border tone for the bottom bar. A palette token (accent, mauve, blue, teal, green, yellow, red, peach/orange, text, dim) follows the theme; anything else is read as a literal colour. Empty uses the warm default.

What the strip is painted on. Unset follows the theme's general background; takes the same names color takes (plus bg and panel), a literal, or reset to show the terminal through. Painted framed or not.
Draw a strip along the bottom edge of the frame.

Two or more colour stops to fade the bottom bar's border between, along its long axis. Stops accept the same palette tokens and literals as `color`. Both ends must carry channel values, so a named terminal colour falls back to `color`.
How many parts anything may put on this bar. Accepted from 1 to 16; anything outside that range is refused rather than clamped, so the file never disagrees with the build.

Whether focus mode quiets the bottom bar. Focus narrows the display to what is being worked in, and a bar that exists to be glanced at is what that mode is asking to be rid of. Off by default, and per edge: the reason to quiet a status strip is not a reason to quiet the strip holding the controls in use. Only the frame is affected — what this file says is still what is stored, so leaving focus brings the bar back.
Thickness of the bottom bar in rows, border included. Values outside 1-32 leave the bar undrawn, and a bordered bar needs at least 3.

Let bar sections draw their glyph icons. Off, a section that names a glyph draws its text instead, and one that names no text is reported rather than left blank. Pictures made of cells (art, pixels) are unaffected. Turn this off for a terminal whose font has no icon glyphs, where they would otherwise render as tofu.

How often a resource or meter section re-reads the machine, in milliseconds. Nothing is read at all unless a section asks for it, so a bar without one costs nothing whatever this says. Accepted between 250 and 60000: below 250 a CPU percentage starts reporting the kernel counter's resolution rather than the machine's load, because the counter ticks a hundred times a second. A value outside the range is reported and the default pace is kept.
